why: p21's sad, glossy loop over deep bass, with its filtered dropout at 2:40 before the beat switch, pulls you into a mood, while p32 is a bright game-level rush circling Am–F with near-identical choruses.

Both are energetic loops that stay at one level, but p22's filtered intro giving way to the full band slamming in at 0:17, and its minor-key major lift at 2:09, land harder than p32's happy, bleepy chiptune drops.
p24's band crashing in after the clean piano intro at 0:21, plus its sad Bm–G–D–A turn at 1:18, beats p34's sinister, relentless Phrygian riff, which never thins out or breaks down.
p24's heavy, sad darkness and its physical arrival at 0:21 outweigh p35's calm, pretty, study-music loop, even with p35's gentle bittersweet swell at 2:12.
p31's drums-only break at 0:11 and the dark, yearning full-band crash at 0:27 pull you in far more than p22's loud, flat three-chord loop, which fills most of its three minutes.
p33's dreamy loop drops in at 0:11 after a dark pad intro and floats through drumless breakdowns at 0:57, while p21 stays wall-to-wall loud and waits until 2:47 for its one big moment.
p25's late-night, bittersweet groove, with the band entering at 0:40 and a drumless middle at 1:15, is far more inviting than p34's uneasy, relentless riffing at one flat loudness.
p23's hush at 0:26 before the full texture sweeps in is a real arrival, even if its climax is heroic and its intro music-box cute, whereas p34 is sinister riffing that never breathes.
p22's band slam at 0:17 and its driving minor-key energy are fun, even if flat, while p35's drumless loop of twinkling piano over G–F#m reads more as gentle focus music than as an immersive swell.
p32's repeated drops and drumless breaks (1:02, 1:25) keep it breathing, while p23 opens with a cute music-box figure and peaks in a heroic loop at constant loudness.
p22's filtered intro, slamming entry and 2:21 breakdown make it an energetic but fun ride, whereas p34's sinister flat-II riff grinds on at one level with no break.
Both have a real arrival, but p31 also breathes, with its drums-alone break at 0:11 and its thinned-out bridge at 1:15, while p24's menacing D–Eb grind stays a wall once the band enters.
p25's late-night, bittersweet lift each cycle and its drumless development at 1:15 have more mood than p32's bright, bleepy two-chord game loop, though both are fairly steady grooves.
p25's hazy intro, solo piano, then the band landing at 0:40 give a cool late-night arc, while p35 cycles a pretty, study-music chord loop for nearly four minutes with only a gentle swell at 2:12.
p35's bittersweet, shimmering swell toward its bright peak at 2:12 feels more immersive than p23's music-box intro and heroic climax loop, though p23's entry at 0:27 hits harder.
p33's hypnotic groove drops in at 0:11 and floats in drumless breakdowns at 0:57, while p23 is a heroic cinematic build that starts with a cute chiming intro.
Both are moody beats, but p31's drums-alone break at 0:11 crashing into yearning chords at 0:27 is a bigger arrival than anything in p21, whose sad loop stays within 2 dB until the 2:47 switch.
p24's heavy, sad band crash at 0:21 and its emotional Bm–G–D–A section at 1:18 beat p32's bright, bleepy game rush, though p24's menacing riff wall keeps the margin small.
p33's dreamy, hypnotic drop-in at 0:11 and its floating drumless breakdowns are fully immersive, while p24's crash-in at 0:21 settles into a menacing wall that barely changes.
p33 pulls you in with its wistful loop landing at 0:11 and its drumless float at 0:57, whereas p22 is a loud game-style rush on one three-chord loop.
p31's dark drums-only break at 0:11 and its yearning crash back in land harder than p25's warm live-band groove, even with p25's nice drumless middle at 1:15.
p21's moody, sad loop over booming bass, with its dropout and beat switch at 2:40–2:47, is cooler than p35's calm, pretty, drumless study-music loop and its gentle swell at 2:12.
p21 is a moody, head-nodding beat with dropouts and a fresh beat switch at 2:47, while p34 is uneasy, relentless riffing that never lets up.
p33's +15 dB drop-in at 0:11 and its hypnotic, floating breakdowns are more immersive than p25's warm, samey live-band groove, which enters at 0:40.
p31's dark, yearning full-band crash after the drums-alone break at 0:11 beats p23's music-box opening and its heroic, static climax loop from 1:08.
